title: Subsampling Bones and Teeth for Ancient DNA Extraction
author: Deon de Jager
materials: Prepare work areas and equipment: Subsampling specimens for aDNA outside a clean lab is not ideal, because it is a non-sterile environment where there is a continual threat from many sources of potential contamination with exogenous DNA. Thus, we take as many precautions as reasonably possible to limit this contamination. This can range from setting up a complete field "clean lab", as in Arrieta-Donato et al. (2025) (see their Supplementary Materials), to simply ensuring the area you are working in is clean and you prevent contamination with your own DNA via bleach, gloves, a mask, and a hairnet. At a minimum: wear two pairs of gloves, a mask, and a hairnet, making sure to change the outer layer of gloves between specimens (to prevent cross-contamination), and clean the work area with 5% bleach solution and 70% ethanol before and after each specimen is subsampled. If possible, also wear disposable sleeves. Follow the same procedures as in Step 9 ( go to step #9 ), excluding the UV cross-linker steps (unless you have one available).
If you brought any materials, e.g. papers or sample bags, with you into the lab, wipe them down with 5% bleach.

Soak drill bits and cutting blades in DNA Away ( DNA AWAY™ Surface Decontaminant Thermo Scientific Catalog #10223471 ) in a small weigh boat for ~10 min . Use 5% bleach solution if DNA Away is not available, but decrease the time to ~2 min.
Clean any other tools/equipment you might use (e.g. mortar, pestle and hammer) with 5% bleach followed by 70% ethanol.
Change your outer layer of gloves.
Remove the equipment and foil from the UV cross-linker that you placed there before starting the subsampling (if 10 min have passed, otherwise wait for the 10 min to be over). These are now sterile.
Once done, clean all surfaces and equipment with 5% bleach followed by 70% ethanol and/or follow the required protocols of the clean lab for post-work clean-up.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Documentation
steps.instruction: Prepare all necessary reagents and equipment, including a printed subsampling table to record specimen data.

substeps.instruction: Print the subsampling table with columns for SampleID, Drill_ID, Date, Mat_group, Target_DNA, Tube_weight (mg), Tube_powder_weight (mg), Weight_DNA (mg), Target_Coll, Weight_Coll (mg), and Notes.
Ensure a separate drill and set of drill bits are available for use outside the clean lab, or thoroughly clean existing ones with 5% bleach and 70% ethanol before entry.

steps.title: Set Up Clean Lab Workspace
steps.instruction: Establish a sterile environment and prepare cleaning solutions.

substeps.instruction: Follow all clean lab contamination-prevention and personal protection procedures, including double-gloving.
Turn on the extractor/fume hood where drilling will occur.
Fill a 250 mL plastic container with 5% bleach solution and soak a disposable cloth in it for surface and specimen cleaning.
Clean all work surfaces with 5% bleach solution followed by 70% ethanol.
Place a large rectangular piece of foil on the subsampling surface and wipe it with 5% bleach to secure it and create a sterile working area.

steps.title: Sterilize Tools and Accessories
steps.instruction: Decontaminate drilling and grinding tools using chemical cleaning and UV irradiation.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the drill down with 70% ethanol, focusing on the area where bits are attached.
Soak drill bits and cutting blades in DNA Away/bleach solution, then dry with tissue paper.
Place a large rectangular piece of foil, the dried drill bits, and the mortar and pestle into the UV cross-linker for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Tubes
steps.instruction: Organize and weigh tubes for powder collection.

substeps.instruction: Label 1.5 or 2mL Eppendorf tubes with Drill_IDs.
Organize specimens in the planned subsampling order.
Weigh the empty Eppendorf tube and record the value as 'Tube_weight' in the table.

steps.title: Prepare Specimen Collection Boat
steps.instruction: Create a sterile vessel to collect bone or tooth powder.

substeps.instruction: Remove the UV-sterilized foil from the cross-linker.
Fold the foil to create a tray or 'boat' with vertical sides to prevent powder loss.

steps.title: Identify and Clean Target Areas
steps.instruction: Select the densest part of the specimen to maximize endogenous DNA yield and clean the surface.

substeps.instruction: For bones: Target the petrous part of the temporal bone (humans) or petrosal bone (mammals), specifically the otic capsule. For long bones, target the outermost layer of the midshaft; avoid spongy (trabecular/epiphyseal) areas.
For teeth: Target the cementum (outer layer of the root), specifically the root tip where cementum is thickened. If available in bovids, target internally secreted cementum in the crown.
Clean the target area by wiping with the bleach-soaked cloth to remove soil/exogenous material, followed by 70% ethanol using tissue paper.
Rinse the cloth in the bleach solution after cleaning the specimen.

steps.title: Subsample Bone or Tooth Material
steps.instruction: Extract powder using drilling or crushing techniques while minimizing heat and contamination.

substeps.instruction: If the bone fragment is very small, crush and grind the entire piece with a mortar and pestle instead of drilling.
When drilling: Use the lowest speed possible and drill in short bursts to prevent heat-induced DNA degradation. Move to new areas with each burst.

When crushing: Use a mortar and pestle (covering the top with one hand to prevent ricochet) or a hammer and protection plate (decontaminated with 5% bleach then 70% ethanol). Place the specimen on UV-sterilized foil folded multiple times to minimize fragment dispersal.
If cementum is 'flaky', collect the flakes and grind them with a mortar and pestle.

steps.title: Collect and Weigh Powder
steps.instruction: Transfer the collected powder to the tube and verify the quantity.

substeps.instruction: Pour the powder into the pre-weighed Eppendorf tube.
Weigh the tube and record as 'Tube_powder_weight'.
Calculate the powder weight (Tube_powder_weight - Tube_weight); ensure at least 50 mg is obtained. If insufficient, subsample more if possible.

steps.title: Subsample for Collagen (Optional)
steps.instruction: Collect additional material for radiocarbon dating or stable isotope analysis.

substeps.instruction: Target bone or tooth dentine (root or crown).
For bone/root, cut off a piece and weigh it in a weigh boat before placing in an Eppendorf or ziploc bag (aim for >250 mg, up to 1000 mg).
For tooth crowns, drill into the dentine and record weights using additional Tube_weight and Tube_coll_weight columns in the table.

steps.title: Decontaminate and Reset for Next Sample
steps.instruction: Clean all equipment and the workspace before processing the next specimen.

substeps.instruction: Return the specimen to its container.
Clean the mortar and pestle with 5% bleach followed by 70% ethanol, ensuring no powder remains.
Clean the drill with 70% ethanol.
Clean the drilling area with 5% bleach followed by 70% ethanol and place a new bleach-wiped piece of foil down.
Remove used drill bits/blades, wipe dry, and ensure no powder is visible (use DNA Away or 5% bleach/70% ethanol if needed).
Place a new piece of foil, the cleaned drill bits, and the mortar and pestle in the UV cross-linker for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Finalize and Store
steps.instruction: Perform final sterilization and store the samples.

substeps.instruction: Treat the final batch of drill bits, blades, and mortar and pestle with the UV cross-linker before storage.
Store subsamples at -20°C or proceed directly to DNA extraction.
Discard used bleach solution according to institutional guidelines.
